Every chronic-care system you've ever seen treats gut dysfunction as a symptom to suppress.

We treat it as a control variable
to continuously manage.

That single reframe — from treatment target to control variable — is the entire intellectual foundation of Orcasho. It makes a feedback loop possible where a static protocol never can be.

The Objective

Most chronic-care systems attempt to create stability by restricting food choices, avoiding triggers, modifying lifestyle, or repeatedly adjusting medications.

Orcasho is designed around
a different objective.

Patient stability despite food variation, medication variation, hormonal changes, travel, and day-to-day life.

The goal is not perfect compliance with a rigid protocol.

The goal is maintaining a consistent physiological response under real-world conditions — even as food intake, medications, schedules, and life circumstances change.

This is why Orcasho operates in continuous 20-day feedback cycles. The protocol adapts to the patient, rather than requiring the patient to continuously adapt to the protocol.

"Patients should not need to organize their lives around their condition. The system should organize itself around the patient."

03 — Intellectual Property

Biochemistry translated into
a feedback algorithm.

This architecture came from fundamental chemistry training applied to human physiology — not from a clinical protocol. The reframe from symptom to control variable is what made it possible to design a feedback loop at all.

Layer 1 — Representation

Patient as a biochemical state vector

Each patient's physiological state is encoded as a 15-dimensional ionic vector. Not symptoms. Not diagnoses. A quantifiable biochemical position that can be compared, measured, and moved directionally.

H⁺ · HCO₃⁻ · Na⁺ · K⁺ · Cl⁻ · Ca²⁺ · Mg²⁺
NH₄⁺ · CO₂ · ROS · pH buffer
O₂⁻ · Zn²⁺ · Fe²⁺/³⁺ · Mn²⁺
Layer 2 — Selection

Compound selection via cosine similarity

Every compound in the library (70–100 substances) carries an ionic signature. The system selects the subset whose combined ionic direction aligns most closely with the patient's target state — pure vector mathematics applied to biology.

target_vector = Σ(symptom_vectors)
score = cosine_similarity(compound_ions, target)
protocol = top_k(score, library)
Layer 3 — Memory

Within-patient intervention-response history

Each 20-day cycle adds a data point: what changed, what the patient's body did, what worked and what didn't. After 10–20 cycles, the system has a longitudinal biochemical fingerprint of that patient that no competitor can replicate without living through the same cycles.

Layer 4 — Scale

Pattern recognition across patients

At 300 patients, individual response patterns are visible. At 3,000, the system begins to predict which protocol modifications will work for a new patient based on biochemical profile similarity. At 30,000, it becomes a predictive infrastructure that cannot be bootstrapped from scratch.

Example: GERD (severity 4→3) target vector — 15 ionic markers

08 — Why This Is Hard to Replicate

Time is the moat.
Biology doesn't run faster with more capital.

A competitor launching today with identical compounds, identical model, and 10× the funding still cannot replicate what Orcasho has — because they would need to live through the same years of within-patient intervention-response cycles to build the dataset. You cannot compress a 20-day biological response cycle. The moat compounds with time, not money.

1 — Executive Summary

Orcasho is a closed-loop biochemical control system that continuously adapts chronic care protocols every 20 days based on real patient feedback. The platform treats digestive biochemical stability as an upstream control variable for chronic disease, operating as a longitudinal care layer between episodic clinical touchpoints.

The evidence base represents approximately 300 real-world patients treated since January 2023. This is not a randomised controlled trial — it is consistent real-world evidence of outcomes across a diverse patient population under bootstrapped, non-institutional conditions. The appropriate next step is a tightly scoped institutional pilot to evaluate deployment feasibility and whether the outcomes replicate within a health system environment.

2 — Population-Level Evidence: 300 Patients

2.1 Primary Outcome: PPI and Antacid Discontinuation

96% of patients have discontinued PPIs and antacids. Patients did not stop PPIs because we told them to — they stopped because the upstream digestive biochemical environment stabilised to the point where acid suppression was no longer required. When digestion and absorption stabilise, the ionic and enzymatic balance that governs acid production normalises. 96% of patients across diverse demographics, conditions, and geographies showed the same pattern.

2.2 Downstream Blood Marker Improvement

Over 70% of patients have shown positive downstream improvements in blood markers beyond their primary gut symptoms. When digestion and absorption stabilise, medications patients are already taking begin to absorb more consistently. Patients with thyroid dysfunction show TSH movements consistent with improved medication processing. Patients with lipid dysregulation show HDL and LDL changes consistent with improved hepatic function. Patients with anaemia show RBC and haemoglobin movement consistent with improved B12 and folate assimilation.

3 — Why These Outcomes Make Mechanistic Sense

Every input — food, medication, supplements, water — follows the same pathway. Mouth → stomach acid → enzymatic hydrolysis → small intestine absorption → blood. Blood is where every clinical measurement happens. If the gut processing environment is unstable, downstream outputs tend to be unstable.

Current chronic care measures and manages outputs. It tracks glucose, TSH, LDL, blood pressure. But it does not systematically stabilise the input processing layer that determines how consistently medications and nutrients actually reach the systems they're meant to affect. Orcasho stabilises that layer. Every 20 days the system measures where the patient's gut processing environment is and adjusts the biochemical protocol to move it toward stability. The 96% PPI discontinuation and 70%+ blood marker improvement are the predictable downstream consequence of fixing the upstream layer.

6 — Proposed Pilot Design

Objective

To evaluate whether Orcasho can function as a structured longitudinal care layer for chronic patients within a health system environment, and to measure whether the downstream improvement pattern observed across 300 real-world patients replicates within a defined institutional pilot cohort over a 9-month observation window.

Proposed Patient Cohort

Primary complaintPersistent GI dysfunction: reflux, bloating, constipation, or upper GI instability
DurationSymptoms present 6+ months with incomplete resolution through standard care
Medication contextCurrently on PPIs, antacids, or other GI medications without full symptom resolution
Age range18 to 70 years
ComorbiditiesMay include thyroid, metabolic, post-treatment profiles — not excluded
ExclusionAcute GI emergency, active malignancy under treatment, pregnancy

Endpoints

Endpoint Type Measurement
Symptom stabilizationPrimaryPatient-reported score at baseline, month 3, 6, 9
PPI and antacid usagePrimaryChange in medication dependency tracked every 3 months
Downstream markersSecondaryAvailable blood markers at baseline, month 3, 6, 9
Patient retentionOperationalPercentage completing full 9-month window
Adverse eventsSafetyAny adverse responses during the pilot
Workflow feasibilityOperationalDashboard engagement and escalation rate
30–50 patients · 9-month window · 13–14 adaptation cycles per patient
Assessment at months 3, 6, 9 · Home-based throughout · Physician dashboard: full visibility
Primary: symptom stabilization + PPI/antacid usage · Secondary: blood marker trends
Integration capex: $0 · No clinic visits required for the Orcasho layer
Clinical

Better chronic stability between visits

Earlier detection of deterioration. Continuous monitoring without adding clinical headcount. Physician dashboard with full visibility at any time.

Operational

Near-zero integration capex

No new hardware, no facility build-out. Software layer on top of existing patient base. 7–8 minutes per patient per month of required physician attention.

Financial

Reduced avoidable utilization

Fewer unmonitored flare-ups means fewer repeat visits, unscheduled endoscopies, and ER escalations driven by inter-visit drift. Capex that doesn't need to be deployed.
